text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

A few days after I was given notice, I wrote to Eva Vogel, the head of Ahornweid Trading Ltd in Basel, and asked her to give me the reasons for the notice in writing. I'm still waiting for anything meaningful.

I'm attaching the e-mails in which I asked the company for the money I'm owed, together with the reply I got, and the first page of my employment contract.

The notice came on 11 May 2026. Ms Vogel called me into her office and gave me a letter ending my employment.

I'm still employed there at the moment, so my job hasn't actually ended yet, let alone half a year ago.

To answer a question my sister asked: I'm not on any staff committee or workers' body at the company. I'm a warehouse supervisor, nothing more.

Why do I think I was let go? Because I asked for what I'm due. For months I worked night shifts without the night supplement that's in my contract, CHF 575 in total. I put that in writing, I was sure I was in the right, and I still am. Ms Vogel was clearly annoyed, and my colleague Tara Bucher heard her say that 'people who come with lists of demands can look for work elsewhere'. Not long after, I had my notice.

I've also attached my pay slip for June.

My notice period hasn't run out yet: it ends on 31 July, and until then I'm still going in to work every day.

What can I do about this, and is it worth it?

Yours faithfully,
Jack Foster
Kirchgasse 77, Basel

attachments.text:
From: Jack Foster
To: Eva Vogel, Ahornweid Trading Ltd
Subject: Night supplement not paid

Dear Ms Vogel

According to my contract I am entitled to a 25% supplement for night work. This supplement has not been paid for my night shifts in the last months. By my calculation the outstanding amount is CHF 575. I ask you to pay this amount with my next salary.

Kind regards
Jack Foster

---

From: Eva Vogel
To: Jack Foster
Subject: RE: Night supplement not paid

Mr Foster, we will look at this. I would ask you not to raise such matters in front of the team.
E. Vogel
